[F4 F10 F11 F14] [RD-5 RD-3]
D3: Segment 1 is separately justified as a reasonable-cause reroute: LTA DataMall records an Accident at 13:52 on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, located 0 m from the optimal route (F18), and Orchard Road was in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 (F15), i.e. severe congestion on the substituted stretch of the optimal route inside the trip window. [F18 F15 F1] [RD-4]
D4: The 14:20–14:24 stationary period (4 min 10 s) is the 7-Eleven stop the rider herself requested at 14:02 ('Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?', F11) and which the driver accepted (F12); it occurred inside segment 2 and is not the driver's own errand. [F2 F11 F12] [RD-3]
D5: The stop location is not the rider's fault in scope terms: the rider named only 'a 7-Eleven', not a place, and nothing in F2 ties the stationary point to Beach Road — the only mention of Beach Road is the driver's own post-trip statement (F14) — so on this record the segment's consent scope cannot be read; if the judge finds the driver alone chose a 7-Eleven that pushed the track off the optimal route without telling the rider the place beforehand, then only that added distance fails to be exempted under RD-3(b) and falls to RD-2. [F11 F2 F14] [RD-3 RD-5]
D6: The waiting line of $1.08 for 4.2 minutes is a metered waiting-unit charge, and for RydeTAXI waiting during the trip is collected on the meter at $0.26/min (F7), so it is not a refundable item under RD-3(c). [F7 F9] [RD-3 RD-2]
D7: The rider's account is long-standing and clean (610 days, rating 4.9, zero disputes and zero upheld in 90 days, F20), and the driver's 90-day history is one upheld no-show and no upheld route dispute (F21); the profile therefore supports no repeated-route-violation finding and no account flag, and profile facts cannot decide the case either way.
